answer: Continuous physical-delay registration requires each agent to submit hardware-attested timing evidence proving sequential work no parallel farm can compress, verified against a shared clock. An attacker running many identities must real-time serialize registrations per machine, so throughput hits a canyon no amount of rented cloud narrows. Each failed attempt forces a costly restart and a slow spiral of retries that multiply wall-clock hours linearly with identity count. One operator cannot fake the garden of independently-timed devices, since forged timestamps fail cross-checks.
